title: Pay Compression Ratio
description:
For each department that has at least two employees with a salary, report the ratio of its highest salary to its lowest, rounded to 2 decimals. Skip departments whose lowest salary is 0 or negative, since the ratio is meaningless there.

Name the columns `department` and `ratio`. Return the result in any order.
solutionSql:
SELECT d.name AS department,
       ROUND(1.0 * MAX(e.salary) / MIN(e.salary), 2) AS ratio
FROM employees e
JOIN departments d ON d.id = e.dept_id
WHERE e.salary IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY d.id, d.name
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2 AND MIN(e.salary) > 0;
hint: Everything you need is in HAVING: both the count check and the guard against a zero or negative denominator.
outputExplanation: Engineering's highest salary is 1.58 times its lowest. Sales' ratio is 1.86. HR has only one salaried employee and is excluded.
schemaSql:
CREATE TABLE departments (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  name TEXT,
  location TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE employees (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  name TEXT,
  title TEXT,
  salary INTEGER,
  dept_id INTEGER,
  manager_id INTEGER,
  hire_date TEXT
);

tests.name: Department with no employees
Employees with NULL department and NULL salary
Single employee, single department
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO departments VALUES (1,'Engineering','Austin');
INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'Solo','Engineer',100000,1,NULL,'2022-04-01');

tests.name: Duplicate names and same hire dates
Zero and negative salaries, boundary dates
Single department with equal salaries — ratio is 1.00

INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'A','X',100,1,NULL,'2020-01-01'),(2,'B','X',100,1,1,'2020-01-01');
